To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Epac-selective cAMP analog 8-pCPC2′-OMe-cAMP- AM stimulates insulin secretion from INS-1 cells and mouse islets and that this action is mediated by PKA.
the AM-ester form of 8-p-CPT-2′ OMe-cAMP is the first Epac-selective cAMP analog that has been shown to activate Rap1 and to stimulate insulin secretion in beta cells.
8-pCpt-2′-OMe-cAMP is a selective activator of Epac, and that Epac contributes to insulin secretion from beta cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of cAMP-binding proteins in beta cells that mediate insulin secretagogue actions of cAMP.
the identification of cAMP-binding proteins that are important for insulin secretion.
the development of cAMP analog probes that are useful to study the biological functions of Epac and PKA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Epac activation is insufficient for the stimulation of insulin secretion in rat INS-1 cells and that PKA activation is required.
the insulin secretagogue properties of 8-p-CPT-2′O-Me-cAMPS are mediated through activation of PKA, whereas those of 8-p-pCPT-AM-cAMPS are due to activation of Epac.
the Epac/PKA ratio is a determinant of the insulin secretagogue potency of cAMP analog-AM-esters in INS-1 and mouse islet cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
8-pCPC-2′-Me-cAMP-AM activates Epac in a glucose metabolism-dependent manner and is a more potent insulin secretagogue than Bt2-cAMP-AM in rat insulinoma cells.
Epac activation, but not PKA activation, is a prerequisite for the insulin secretagogue actions of cAMP in rat INS-1 cells.
the AM-ester derivative of the Epac-selective cAMP analog 8-pCPCPT-2′O-Me-cAMPhas enhanced biological activity and insulin secretagogue properties compared with its non-AM-derivative.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AM-esters of cAMP analogues can be used to selectively activate Epac or to selectively activate PKA in cells, including beta cells.
the use of AM-esters of cAMP analog is essential to achieve selective activation of Epac in beta cells.
the AM-ester derivative of 8-pCTP-2′-Me-cAMP is a potent and selective activator of Epac, and that this analog may be useful for the study of cAMP signaling in beta cells.
